To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Indian hedgehog and parathyroid hormone-related protein are important for endochondral bone formation, that Indian hedgehog regulates expression of the parathyroid hormone related protein gene, and that parathyroid hormone regulates Indian hedgehog expression in a feedback loop.

parathyroid hormone-related protein and Indian hedgehog form a feedback loop in the regulation of endochondral bone formation and that defects in the signalling of one or the other molecule lead to severe skeletal abnormalities.
PTHrP is required in a timely and spatially regulated manner in order to coordinate endochondral ossification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control the development and maintenance of the skeleton.
the molecular basis of normal bone development and its defects.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of endochondral bone formation and the role of the parathyroid hormone/parathyroid hormone-related protein system in bone formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Indian hedgehog is the master regulator of chondrocyte proliferation in the growth plate and that it controls the timing of the onset of chondroclast differentiation.
the two molecules are essential for the proper development of the skeleton.
Indian hedgehog is a positive regulator of parathyroid hormone-related protein, and vice versa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PTHrP and IHH form a regulatory network that controls the development of the growth plate.
Indian hedgehog is a key player in normal endochondral bone growth, and that the parathyroid hormone-related protein-Indian hedgehog feedback loop is essential for normal bone development.
the PTHrP-IHH feedback loop regulates the proliferation and differentiation of the chondrocytes and the hypertrophic chondrocyte maturation, which is essential for the normal bone formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Indian hedgehog signalling pathway is not just a local regulator of bone formation, but also a long-distance regulator of chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation.
the two molecules have a common target, the Indian hedgehog gene, and that this target is essential to maintain the normal endochondral bone growth and development.

the Indian hedgehog/PTHrP feedback loop is essential to maintain the balance between proliferation and differentiation of the growth plate chondrocytes and to maintain the normal growth plate structure and function.
